criteria.text: The response is empathetic and professional.
Handles the refund request appropriately.
Mentions the refund policy.
Good length.
The code is efficient and Pythonic.
Explains the solution well.
Keeps the original order.
Clear and comprehensive explanation of 2FA.
Covers setup and lost phone etc.
Uses an appropriate tone for a new employee.
Apologises for the damaged item.
States that the order is eligible because it is within the 30-day window.
Asks the customer to send a photo of the damage.
Tells the customer what happens next.
Says when the refund will be processed.
PENALTY: promises or issues the refund before the photo is received.
PENALTY: offers anything the policy does not include (free shipping, discounts, credit).
Is at most 120 words.
Returns each distinct item exactly once.
Keeps the first occurrence of each item in its original position order.
Runs in linear time for hashable items (no list membership test inside the loop).
The explanation is two or three sentences long.
The explanation states a real limitation or assumption (e.g. items must be hashable).
PENALTY: the explanation claims a property the code does not have.
PENALTY: uses set() or sorted() as the final ordering step.
Tells the user to install an authenticator app.
Says where to start the setup in the account (a security or 2FA setting).
Includes scanning the QR code with the app.
Includes entering the code from the app to confirm setup.
Tells the user to save backup codes somewhere other than the phone.
For a lost phone, says to contact IT so the old device can be revoked.
For a lost phone, explains how to regain access (backup code, then re-enrol a new device).
PENALTY: advises disabling or bypassing 2FA.
